Aorsi.fact: Yancai was centered near the Aral Sea and able to muster 100,000 mounted archers.

Aorsi.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Aorsi.question: Y. A. _____ suggests that the subjugation of Yancai by Kangju occurred in the 1st century BC
Aorsi.fact: Y. A. Zadneprovskiy suggests that the subjugation of Yancai by Kangju occurred in the 1st century BC.

Aorsi.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Aorsi.question: This migration contributed significantly to the _____ in Europe, which played an important role in world history
Aorsi.fact: This migration contributed significantly to the Migration Period in Europe, which played an important role in world history.

Aorsi.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Aorsi.question: In the 1st century AD, the Alans achieved a dominant position among the _____ living between the Don River and the Caspian Sea
Aorsi.fact: The westward expansion of Kangju obliged many of the Aorsi and other Sarmatians to migrate westwards. In the 1st century AD, the Alans achieved a dominant position among the Sarmatians living between the Don River and the Caspian Sea.

Aorsi.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Aorsi.question: Ptolemy also speaks of the _____, suggesting that a fusion of some sorts between them had occurred
Aorsi.fact: Ptolemy also speaks of the Alanorsi, suggesting that a fusion of some sorts between them had occurred.

Aorsi.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Aorsi.question: The most important contemporaneous source on the Aorsi was the Greek geographer Strabo, in Geographica (_____/63 BC – c
Aorsi.fact: The most important contemporaneous source on the Aorsi was the Greek geographer Strabo, in Geographica (64/63 BC – c.

Aorsi.subject: Indian Wildlife & National Parks
Aorsi.question: The 2nd century BC diplomat Zhang Qian (cited by Sima Qian in Chapter 123 of the Shiji), reported that Yancai lay 2,000 li (_____) north-west of the state of Kangju, in the Ferghana Valley, with which
Aorsi.fact: The 2nd century BC diplomat Zhang Qian (cited by Sima Qian in Chapter 123 of the Shiji), reported that Yancai lay 2,000 li (832 km) north-west of the state of Kangju, in the Ferghana Valley, with which it shared similar customs.
